courses.label: ENGL 410A
courses.title: Satire and Sense: The Restoration and Early 18th Century
paras: The Restoration comedy of manners, heroic and high tragedy, poetry of the court wits and other amused commentators on society, and the major writings of Dryden, Swift, Addison, Defoe, and the early Pope.

courses.label: ENGL 410B
courses.title: Sense and Sensibility: The Middle and Later 18th Century
paras: The probing of mores and manners by Pope and Johnson, the emergence of the novel with Fielding and Sterne, and the transformation (in “the age of sensibility”) of literary attitudes and practice from classical to romanticism.

courses.label: ENGL 430A
courses.title: The Romantic Movement 1
paras: The poetry and critical theory of Blake, Wordsworth, and Coleridge. Emphasis is primarily on poetry; selected minor writers may be considered.

courses.label: ENGL 430B
courses.title: The Romantic Movement 2
paras: The poetry and critical theory of Byron, Shelley, and Keats. Emphasis is primarily on poetry; selected minor writers may be considered.

courses.label: ENGL 451A
courses.title: Literature of the Victorian Age 1
paras: An historical and critical study of major poets (Browning, Tennyson, Arnold) and of the literary criticism of the period.

courses.label: ENGL 451B
courses.title: Literature of the Victorian Age 2
paras: An historical and critical study of major novelists (Dickens, Thackeray, Eliot) and major essayists (Newman, Ruskin, Mill, Huxley).

courses.label: ENGL 460A
courses.title: British Literature, 1885-1918
paras: A study of works by such writers as Shaw, Conrad, and Yeats.

courses.label: ENGL 460B
courses.title: British Literature, 1918-1945
paras: A study of works by such writers as James Joyce, D.H. Lawrence, and T.S. Eliot.

courses.label: ENGL 470A
courses.title: Contemporary Critical Theory
paras: An examination of recent influential critical theories. Among the schools studied will be feminist criticism, Marxist criticism, psycholanalytic criticism and, especially, deconstruction.

courses.label: ENGL 470B
courses.title: History of Literary Criticism
paras: An historical survey of major critical texts and movements from the Greek and Roman classics to the New Criticism of the mid-20th century, examining different critical theories and practices in a context of cultural changes.

courses.label: ERS 100
courses.title: Issue Analysis and Problem Solving for Environmental Studies 1
paras: Designed to complement the introductory overview of ENV S 195 and the introduction to methods and techniques (ERS 150). Selected themes and case examples are analyzed within a framework of concepts and theories from the natural and social sciences. Students undertake practical exercises to develop analytic and problem-solving skills.
Prereq: Environment and Resource Studies students only

courses.label: ERS 101
courses.title: Issue Analysis and Problem Solving for Environmental Studies 2
paras: Continuation of ERS 100.
Prereq: Environment and Resource Studies students only

courses.label: ERS 150
courses.title: Environmental Issues: Methods and Techniques
paras: Course will teach basic research skills to complement the problem-solving skills taught in ERS 100/101. Concentration on the “systems approach” and its use in problem soiving, with attention to information gathering and organization, quantitative data analysis techniques, and presentation skills. Microcomputers will be used for report generation, information organization and basic data analysis.
Prereq: Environment and Resource Studies students only

courses.label: ERS 218
courses.title: Introduction to Sustainable Environmental and Resource Systems
paras: Examination of patterns and trends in major environmental systems and natural resource use. Analysis of these resources in the context of sustainable development. Local, regional and global systems will be examined.
Prereq: At least second-year standing

courses.label: ERS 231
courses.title: Environmental Issues in a Global Perspective
paras: This course examines the various political, economic and social factors in development and environmental concerns in various Third World countries. Special focus is on health-care systems, agricultural and forestry practices and policies, water management and resource ownership. Students are encouraged to study one country in some depth, and to submit seminars and projects.
Prereq: ENV S 195 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 241
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Social impact Assessment
paras: An introduction to means of assessing proposed approaches to environmentally and socially significant problems and opportunities. Special emphasis on the nature and limitations of conventional means of assessing the impacts, and overall desirability of technologies, projects, plans and policies. Close examination of case examples. Prereq: At least second-year standing

courses.label: ERS 275A
courses.title: Special Readings
paras: Background reading and study in consultation with Faculty. Typically utilized when a student must study a topic in connection with other work, but no course offering that topic is available.
Prereq: Consent of instructor
The letter designation allows this course to be taken more than once for credit

courses.label: ERS 280
courses.title: Applied Field Studies
paras: Analysis of selected environmental issues or programs with particular emphasis on applied problem-solving/ management perspectives. Field trips to chosen sites will be conducted to gather information for analysis. Key organizations/people will be involved in field trips and discussions.
Field trip fee $45 per student

courses.label: ERS 290
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Individual or small group project emphasizing multidisciplinary treatment of environmental probiems. Work encouraged on situations of interest to community organizations, government agencies or other groups.
Prereq: Students with second-year standing in Environment and Resource Studies

courses.label: ERS 291
courses.title: Seminar-Workshop
paras: Continuation of project begun in ERS 290
Prereq: ERS 290

courses.label: ERS 295
courses.title: Development of Environmental Thought 1
paras: Examination of conflicting positions on how we do and should view the natural world and ourselves, beginning with review of the history of attitudes to the environment and our place in it. Emphasis on evolution of attitudes to human nature and the environment in industrial sociaty, critiques of these attitudes and implications for approaches to modern environmental issues. Prereq: Environment and Resource Studies students only with at least second-year standing or consent of instructor
Course Descriptions Environment and Resource Studies

courses.label: ERS 305
courses.title: Ecosystem Perspectives and Analyses
paras: Examination of the concept of the “ecosystem” presented in recent writings about non-equilibrium thermodynamics, ecological paradigms, conservation biology and environmental philosophy. Discussion of the theoretical and practical implications of these contrasting perspectives for issues of research/environmental management and sustainable development.
Prereq: ENV S 200, at least thirdyear standing, or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 318
courses.title: Case Studies in Sustainabie Environmental and Resource Systems
paras: Detailed analysis of selected environmental systems and resource use activities. Particular attention will be given to opportunities for sustainable development and issues in implementation. Case studies will be drawn from local, regional and international experiences. Prereq: Third-year standing and ERS 218 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 337
courses.title: Biophysical Impact Assessment
paras: Major problems and issues in the management of environmental impacts stemming from development projects. Synthesis of ecological, economic and institutional aspects. Integrating environmental management with social and economic development policies and programs.
Prereq: ERS 241 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 338
courses.title: Socioeconomic Impact Assessment
paras: Introduction to the background, theory and methodology of social impact assessment (SIA). SIA as a type of - social science research and as a key element in achieving more informed and responsible decision-making in society. Experience in SIA design for environmentally-relevant cases.
Prereq: ERS 241 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 352
courses.title: Current issues in the Canadian North
paras: Introduction to contemporary environmental, social, economic and political issues in Canada's North, principally Yukon, Northwest Territories and Northern Quebec and Labrador. Lectures and tutorials will discuss homeland and frontier perspectives, economic development and environmental conservation, the northern economies, native land claims and political development.
Prereq: At least second-year standing

courses.label: ERS 361
courses.title: International Communication System and Development
paras: Information and ideas constitute the most basic resource of a people. This course will explore the role of various mass media, newspapers, We cinema, magazines, radio, travellers, in the process of development. What is the nature of mass education in a developing society? How do the media hinder or contribute to social change? These and many related questions will be explored in the context of a number of different societies.
Prereq: At least second-year standing or consent of instructor

courses.title: Technology/Lifestyles fora Conserver Society What is a Conserver Society? What
paras: must we do to make our society into a Conserver Society? How do we evaluate the appropriateness of a lifestyle. or technology for a Conserver Society? Is a Conserver Society realistic? This course will explore these questions, with emphasis on student participation in discussion and in seminar presentations. Lectures will focus on the basics of various technologies and lifestyles, and on quantitative techniques for comparing these.
Prereq. At least second-year standing

Assessment of alternative futures. Prereq: ERS 295 and third-year standing or consent of instructor

courses.title: Senior Honours Seminar
paras: Provides practice in applying skills that are useful to people working in different kinds of organizations. Readings, discussions and exercises emphasize: problem perceptions and diagnoses, actor system analyses, and planning, management and evaluation activities as these are carried out by and within organizations. Special attention given to roles that persons having an environmental studies-background may be particularly well prepared to develop and refine.
Prereq: Fourth-year Environment and Resource Studies students only or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 418
courses.title: Seminar on Strategies for Sustainable Development
paras: Using selected environmental systems and resource use activities the course will analyse selected policy, planning and implementation strategies for sustainable development. The analysis will include consideration of organizational and institutional arrangements. Various approaches reflecting local, regional and international experiences will be compared and contrasted. Prereq: Fourth-year standing and ERS 318 or consent of instructor

courses.label: ERS 445
courses.title: Impact Assessment and Policy Analysis: Practicum
paras: Students will draw on knowledge and experience gained in the prerequisite theme courses to critique and/or design impact analyses of a variety of “realworld” activities, including policy initiatives, technological choices, environmentally-relevant proposals, economic strategies and others of special interest or significance. Prereq: ERS 241, 337 and 338, or consent of instructor

Introductory Note

There are a number of courses offered in the Faculty of Environmental Studies of an integrative nature which extend across the academic interests of the four units: School of Architecture, Department of Geography, Department of Environment and Resource Studies, and School of Urban and Regional Planning. The courses are of a general interest and are open to all students in the University. There is not an actual

Students interested in this area are urged to consult the course offerings of the four individual units mentioned above. These four departments/schools offer a variety of related courses allowing in depth studies of topics covered in the Environmental Studies courses.

courses.label: ENVS 178
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Research Methods
paras: {introduction to methods of developing, evaluating and using evidence in Environmental Studies. Methods for summarizing and critical appreciation of data describing environmental systems. Skill development in applying statistical techniques and in using microcomputers as a research tool.
While not a prerequisite for this course, CS 100 or a high school computing course is helpful.

courses.label: ENVS 195
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental Studies
paras: Provides an overview of human ecological aspects of environmental studies from an intercultural and global perspective.
Course Descriptions Environmental Studies

courses.label: ENVS 200
courses.title: Field Ecology
paras: Introduces the main concepts and principles of ecology; the cycling of elements; energetics and structural organization of major ecological systems; population dynamics; impact of natural resource management practices and urban and industrial development on the environment; incorporating environmental quality considerations into development activities. The laboratory sessions include field trips to study natural and disturbed ecosystems, urban and applied ecology.
Prereq: Second, third and fourth year students only
Lab fee of $5
Students may receive credit for only one of ENV S 200 and BIOL 250

courses.label: ENVS 201
courses.title: Introduction to Environmental and Planning Law
paras: Introduction to legal concepts generally and to environmental and planning law concepts in particular. Designed both for students who do not plan to take further in depth legal courses and as a prerequisite for senior iegal courses - ENV S 401 and PLAN 402. Topics to be covered include Sources of Law, Nature of Legal Remedies, Common Law, Administrative Agencies, Planning Act, Environmental Protection and Assessment Acts, and Federal Environmental Protection Act.

courses.label: ENVS 220
courses.title: Environmental Economics
paras: Evaluation of various economic approaches to the environment. The links between economics, systems and the natural environment will be explored and future directions examined.

courses.label: ENVS 252
courses.title: Media Tools for Environmental Studies
paras: Instruction in basic black and white photography relating to photography's role as a media tool; basic darkroom functions, camera operation, composition, photographic theory, and photo essay production. Much of the course work and projects will be done outside the classroom in field situations of environmental concern using initiative in project development. Students are expected to supply their own cameras. A limited number of cameras will be available on a rental basis.

courses.label: FR 151
courses.title: Basic French 1
paras: For students with some elementary or secondary school French not exceeding Year Two (Grade Ten in Ontario) or equivalent. Emphasizes comprehension, grammar and basic speaking skills.
Antireq: Ontario Grade 11 French or equivalent. See above, notes 1-6

courses.label: FR 152
courses.title: Basic French il
paras: A continuation of the work done in FR 151. Prereq: FR 151 or equivalent Antireq: Ontario Grade 12 French or equivalent

courses.label: FR 155
courses.title: Intermediate French Language |
paras: A comprehensive study of French grammar and vocabulary. invoives reading, writing and speaking French. Prereq: FR 152 or Ontario Grade 12 French or equivalent Antireg: Ontario Grade 13 or Ontario Academic Course French or equivalent. See above, notes 1-6

courses.label: FR 156
courses.title: Intermediate French Language Ill
paras: A continuation of the work done in FR 155.
Prereq: FR 155

courses.label: FR 192A
courses.title: Advanced French Language 1A
paras: An intensive French Language course. Emphasis will be placed on strengthening oral expression, comprehension of spoken French, reading and writing skills.
Prereq: Ontario Grade 13 or Ontario Academic Course French or equivalent. See above, notes 1-6
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: FR 192B
courses.title: Advanced French Language IB
paras: Continuation of FR 192A.
Prereq: FR 192A
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: FR 193
courses.title: French for Francophone Students 1

Prereq: Consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 201
courses.title: Advanced French Language IC
paras: A transitional course, enabling students at the Intermediate level in Year | to join the Advanced stream of language courses. Students who successfully complete this course may continue to FR 250.
Prereq: FR 156 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 208D
courses.title: Spoken French Through Drama
paras: A course which will use the rehearsal and performance of a play in French as a basis for intensive oral training. Students will participate in the preparation of the play, and also do a project related to the play.
Prereq: FR 250, FR 250A or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 250
courses.title: Advanced French Language 2
paras: Continued intensive study of spoken and written French, with emphasis on more difficult problems of the language. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 192A and FR 192B or FR 195 and FR 196 or FR 201 or consent of the Department.

courses.label: FR 250A
courses.title: Advanced Spoken French 2

Prereq: FR 250

courses.label: FR 255
courses.title: Business French
paras: A French language course designed to enable the student to carry on standard business practices in spoken and written French.
Prereq: FR 192A/B, 195/196, 201 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 293
courses.title: French for Francophone Students 2
paras: A second level course for francophones and near-fluent speakers of French. in addition to continued emphasis on correct usage, attention will be paid to stylistic improvement.
Prereq: FR 193 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 300
courses.title: Advanced French Language 3
paras: Intensive development of writing skills through a study of stylistics and translation. Advanced oral composition will also be emphasized. Taught in French. Prereq: FR 250 or FR 251 and FR 252 or FR 293 or consent of the Department
Course Descriptions French

courses.label: FR 300A
courses.title: Advanced Spoken French 3
paras: An advanced level course intended to continue intensive oral and aural skill development. Taught in French.

paras: Intensive development of advanced
comparative stylistics, transiation and

LINGUISTICS COURSES

courses.title: Introduction to the Phonetics of
paras: French
This course introduces the student on a
practical level to the phonetic system of
contemporary French, and on a theoret-
ical level to a phonological description
of that system. Taught in French. Prereg: FR 192A and FR 192B or FR
195 and FR 196

courses.label: FR 303

paras: This course will introduce students to a
basic theoretic rettection on language.
Various important schools of modern
linguistic thought ranging from Saus-
sure to Chomsky, etc. will be

courses.label: FR 403
courses.title: Topic in Linguistics
paras: An area in Linguistics of particular interest to the Instructor and the students will be chosen. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 250 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 409
courses.title: Medieval French Language
paras: Introduction to the early development of French.
CIVILIZATION COURSES
Language of Instruction.

Courses are normally taught in French. However, in the case of students not enrolled in a French Major or Honours Program, permission may be given for written assignments and examinations to be done in English.

courses.label: FR 263
courses.title: Aspects of France
paras: An examination of contemporary French society through documents taken from different media.
Prereq: FR 192 or consent of the Department
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: FR 273
courses.title: Aspects of Quebec
paras: A presentation of traditional and contemporary Quebec in the fields of the Arts, literature, music, politics and society. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 192, 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 291
courses.title: French Civilization 1
paras: This course traces the cultural development of France from its origin to the French Revolution. Emphasis is given to the study of music, art, architecture, literature, ideas and “daily life” in their historical context.
See Note under FR 292.

courses.label: FR 292
courses.title: French Civilization 2
paras: This course completes the study of the cultural development of France to 1900. After that, the course emphasizes a study of life in these two areas today. Considerable attention will be paid to art, politics, industry, etc. Prereq: FR 291 is recommended FR 291 and 292 are taught in English. Open to Arts students in second year and higher, and to others in any year. Students in a French Major, Honours, or Minor Program are encouraged to take this course as an elective.

courses.label: FR 393A
courses.title: French Civilization, 1884-1914
paras: Offered in the Nantes Program.

courses.label: FR 395A
courses.title: French Thought
paras: A survey of the principal thinkers and currents of ideas in France from the Renaissance to the Present. Offered in the Nantes Program.
LITERATURE COURSES
Language of Instruction.

Courses are normally taught in French. However, in the case of students not enrolled in a French Major or Honours Program, permission may be given for written assignments and examinations to be done in English.

FRI95A 3C 0.5 French Studies 1 A survey of French civilization and literature prior to the 18th century and an introduction to the discipline. Language skills will be developed through dictées, composition and written assignments. Taught in French.
Prereq: OAC or Grade 13 French or equivalent
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: FR 196
courses.title: French Studies 2
paras: A survey of French civilization and literature frdm the 18th century to the present. Continued emphasis on language skills through dictées, composition and written assignments. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 or FR 192A or consent of the Department
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: FR 231
courses.title: Survey of 17th-Century French Literature
paras: This course will trace the development of French literature from 1600-1700. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 232
courses.title: Topics and Problems in 17th-Century French Literature
paras: A more detailed study of writers/works of the classical period. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department
Course Descriptions French

courses.label: FR 253
courses.title: Romanticism
paras: This course wiil deal with French literature between 1789 and 1848. This course will explore the principal literary movement of this period: Romanticism. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 264
courses.title: 20th-Century French Theatre
paras: The study of a representative number of authors and texts from Claudel to lonesco. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 275
courses.title: Contemporary French-Canadian Novel
paras: A study of a limited number of texts by authors such as Gabrielle Roy, André Langevin, Hubert Aquin, Gérard Bessette. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 342
courses.title: 18th-Century French Literature
paras: This course will trace the development of French literature from 1700-1800. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department
Also offered at St. Jerome's College.

courses.label: FR 343
courses.title: Topics and Problems in 18th-Century French Literature
paras: A more detailed study of one or more aspects of the Enlightenment. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 354
courses.title: Realism and Naturalism
paras: This course will study the literature from 1848 to 1900. It will cover not only the major writers but also the theories behind the social, artistic and intellectual trends in this part of the century. Prereg: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department Not open to students who have taken FR 254.

courses.label: FR 363
courses.title: 20th-Century French Novel
paras: A survey of the Novel from Proust to the present day through the study of a selection of Key Texts. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 371
courses.title: French-Canadian Poetry
paras: A study of its evolution from Octave Crémazie to Anne Hébert and the present. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 372
courses.title: Contemporary Quebec Theatre
paras: A study of contemporary Quebec theatre, from Gratien Gélinas to the present. Taught in French
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 391
courses.title: French Women Writers
paras: A study of selected works by women writers in France from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century. The course will focus on the literary features of these works and on their value as reflections of the position of women in French society throughout the period. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 410
courses.title: Medieval French Literature
paras: An introduction to French literature of the Middle Ages through the study of representative texts, including excerpts from the epic, courtly and satirical works. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 423
courses.title: Survey of 16th Century French Literature
paras: A study of French authors of the Renaissance (1500-1600). Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 424
courses.title: Topics and Problems in 16th Century French Literature
paras: A focussed study of a particular theme of Renaissance (1500-1600) writing. Taught in French.
Prereq: FR 195 or FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 451
courses.title: Symbolist Poetry
paras: The course will concentrate on the works of four poets — Baudelaire, Verlaine, Rimbaud and Mallarmé. Special emphasis will be placed on the “explication de texte” as a technique in the analysis of poetry.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 482
courses.title: Study of Individual Authors
paras: Each year a different author is the
subject of specialized study to permit
an in depth exploration of his/her
literary qualities. Taught in French. Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or
consent of the Department

courses.label: FR 483
courses.title: French Literary Criticism
paras: An introduction to modern critical theoties. A study of concepts and methods from semiotic, psychoanalytic and sociological approaches.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Deparment
Students intending to proceed to graduate studies in French are particularly advised to take this course.

courses.label: FR 490
courses.title: Senior Tutorials
paras: A small group of students follows a course of study under the supervision of a faculty member. For details, inquire of the Department.
Prereq: FR 195 and FR 196 or consent of the Department

courses.label: GEOG 101
courses.title: Introduction to Human Geography
paras: An introduction to human geography through a survey of some of the concepts, methods, techniques and applications of geographic analysis to the human cultural environment. Directed towards people-land and iocation analysis themes.

courses.label: GEOG 102
courses.title: Introduction to Physical Geography
paras: Emphasis on the natural environment as an integrated system. Selected aspects of weather — climate, water, soils, biota, landforms along with flows of energy, water and matter and their effects on the subsystems of the natural environment.
Course Descriptions French Geography

courses.label: GEOG 120
courses.title: The World Region
paras: Selected areas of the world's climatic regions, emphasizing characteristic problems as well as their physical, cultural and economic interrelationships, resources use, population pressure, urban and rural land use, and human impact on the earth.

courses.label: GEOG 160
courses.title: Introduction to Cartography and Map Analysis
paras: Basic concepts involved in the analysis and use of existing types of cartographic products. Background theory of the production and reproduction of topographic and thematic maps, including historical development, collection of data and symbolization.
Lab fee $15-$25.

courses.label: GEOG 201
courses.title: Geomorphology and Soils
paras: The roles of geomorphological and soil forming processes in creating and modifying landscapes. The utility of geomorphological information in our everyday lives.
Prereq: GEOG 102

courses.label: GEOG 202A
courses.title: Location of Economic Activities
paras: The locational structure of economic activities in the context of regional development, with the use of case studies. Basic concepts and tools are used to analyse the location structure of primary, secondary and tertiary activities.
Prereq: A first-year human geography course or equivalent

courses.label: GEOG 202B
courses.title: The Geography of Economic Development
paras: This course focuses upon the integrative nature of economic development through analysis of space-time relationships at different scales of geographic analysis (community, regional, national and international).
Prereq: GEOG 202A

courses.label: GEOG 205
courses.title: Africa
paras: The geogpraphy of modern Africa south of the Sahara in the context of changing attitudes to the continent on the part of “developed” countries. Attention will focus on problems of the physical, social and economic environments.

courses.label: GEOG 208
courses.title: Applied Climatology
paras: World climate and weather patterns and their impact on humanity. Topics include atmospheric circulation, climate classifications, air pollution, urban climate, climate change and weather modification.
Prereq: GEOG 102

courses.label: GEOG 220
courses.title: The World Region and World Issues
paras: This course will discuss specific world regions, e.g., Japan, Switzerland, E. Europe, U.S.S.R., within a global context. It will also discuss world issues, including some of the following topics: the underdeveloped world, energy, the spread of arms and terrorism, environmental degradation, world trade, the flow of capital, and integrating geographical elements within the world region.

courses.label: GEOG 225
courses.title: Urbanization in the Third World
paras: An analysis of the factors behind the rapid urbanization of selected areas in Asia, Africa and Latin America, with an examination of related problems of urban planning and development control policies.
Prereq: Any Faculty of Environmental Studies course or Third Worid Development course.
Cross-listed as PLAN 225
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 225 and PLAN 225.

courses.label: GEOG 227
courses.title: Regional Problems of Europe
paras: An introduction to the Geography of Europe which examines agricultural, industrial and urban problems. Lectures, discussions and visual presentations based on field experience of instructors.

courses.label: GEOG 275
courses.title: Introductory Air Photo Analysis and Remote Sensing
paras: Basic characteristics of various remote sensing techniques and their application in the broad field of geographic and environmental studies. Emphasis on the analysis and interpretation of air photos in 3 dimensions.
Lab fee $20.

courses.label: GEOG 300
courses.title: Geomorphology and the Southern Ontario Environment
paras: Study of the origin and evolution of land forms of Southern Ontario. Analysis of contemporary geomorphic processes. Study of human impact on geomoarphological landscapes. The lectures will be supplemented by field trips and field work required for term projects.
Prereq: Third and fourth year Students only with GEOG 201 or consent of instructor
Lab tee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 302
courses.title: Geomorphological Processes
paras: The impact of processes in landform development and modification. Methodologies for measuring landform changes over different time periods and under different climatic conditions. Processes discussed in detail will include two or more of the following: Glaciation and De-glaciation, Fluvial, Aeolian, Karst, Coastal and Human Activity.
Prereq: GEOG 201 or EARTH 121/122 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 303
courses.title: Geographical Hydrology
paras: Study of the land based hydrological cycle and water balance with Canadian emphasis. Focus on snowcover, glacier ice, ground ice, streams and lakes and their physical, ecological and socioeconomic significance.
Prereq: GEOG 201 and one of GEOG 208 or 309

courses.label: GEOG 304
courses.title: Field and Lab Techniques in Geomorphology
paras: An analysis of the range of techniques used by geomorphologists. This course will involve intensive field surveying, mapping and laboratory work.
Prereq: GEOG 300 or EARTH 342 or consent of instructor
Field-trip expenses: $15 per student

courses.label: GEOG 307
courses.title: Social Survey Techniques
paras: Social research and the planning process, interview and seif administered surveys; questionnaire design; profile data; sampling; data processing; nonsurvey data collection techniques; practical applications.
Prereq: Second- or third-year students with ENV S 178 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as PLAN 307
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 307 and PLAN 307.
Estimated additional cost to student: 10
Course Descriptions Geography

courses.label: GEOG 311
courses.title: Regional and Local Development
paras: Economic development at regional and local scales. Emphasis on theoretical frameworks, empirical studies and planning issues.
Prereq: GEOG 202A and GEOG 202B or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 316
courses.title: Multivariate Statistics
paras: The theory and application of multivariate statistics, with particular emphasis upon the use of the computer.
Prereq: ENV S 278 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as PLAN 316
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 316 and PLAN 316

courses.label: GEOG 320
courses.title: Regional Geography
paras: The approach of the regional geographer is illustrated using one or more specific regions. Political, social and historical processes are studied as they affect perception of the regional environment. Example regions used are Austria, Alpine and Mediterranean World, Greece, Hungary, Switzerland. Prereq: A first-year human geography course.

courses.label: GEOG 322
courses.title: Geographical Study of Canada Geographical basis of Canada and
paras: Canadian issues. Selected problems relating to nationalism, regionalism, environmental quality, urbanization, tegional disparities and resource devalopment.

courses.label: GEOG 323
courses.title: Perspective on International Tourism
paras: The character, problems of, and prospects for tourism are examined through consideration of tourism in a variety of countries and regions, both developed and developing. Topics include the nature and significance of tourism; economic, environmental and social impacts of tourism; and costs and benefits of tourism to destination area. Prereg: GEOG 202A, REC 230 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 326
courses.title: Gender Roles and Development Alternatives in the Third World
paras: The course examines several conceptual research methods and action approaches, ranging from conventional development theories to feminist perspectives; from planning (macro and micro level) and program developments for women to popular, grass-root community movements in the development processes at work.
Prereq: First- or Second-year Third World Development courses

courses.label: GEOG 332
courses.title: Health and Disease in the Third World
paras: Geographic concepts and issues in studying health related problems. Topics include: morbidity and mortality patterns, “population at risk", malnutrition, poverty, access to modern health care, and alternative health care systems, Regional case studies from the developing countries (seminar method).
Prereq: Second-year Third World Development courses or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 349
courses.title: The City as a System
paras: Theories, models, and research procedures in the study of internal urban structure. Focuses on city-wide processes, urban land use, spatial economics, interaction systems, decision-making, urban growth, and the processes of development and redevelopment.
Prereq: GEOG 202A or 251 or consent of instructor
Field trip fee $5-$10

courses.label: GEOG 350
courses.title: Regional Urban Systems
paras: Theories, models and research procedures dealing with the growth and support of urban centres and city systems and their role in regional development.
Prereq: GEOG 202A or GEOG 251 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 353
courses.title: Marketing Geography
paras: Emphasized are consumer behaviour, firm organization and behaviour, and modelling and analysis of commercial location patterns at both inter- and intra-urban scales.
Prereq: GEOG 202A

courses.label: GEOG 356
courses.title: Resources Management
paras: Reviews selected theories, methods, and terminology related to economic, behavioural, institutional and decisionmaking aspects of resources and environmental problems.
Prereq: ENV S 178 or consent of instructor
Field Trip fee $10-$15

courses.label: GEOG 358
paras: Water Planning and Management: Strategies and Experiences Benchmark theory and principles of comprehensive water planning and integrated river basin management. Selected international to local scale case studies.
Prereq: Consent of instructor
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 367
courses.title: Conservation in Wildland and Resource Management
paras: Consideration of the constraints and guidelines that an application ofthe principles of ecology place on the planning and management of resources within natural and agricultural ecosystems. The theory and history of this subject will be discussed together with the management of wildlife, forestry, fisheries, parks and open space, and agriculture..
-Prereq: ENV S 200
Cross-listed as PLAN 367
Lab fee $10-15
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 367 and PLAN 367

courses.label: GEOG 368
courses.title: Conservation/Resource Management of the Built Environment
paras: Consideration of the constraints and guidelines that an application of the principles of ecology place on the pianning and management of resources within urban and urban shadow ecosystems. The theory and history of this subject will be discussed together with urban ecomanagement, the management of waste, urban open space and parks, rehabilitated sites, and environmentally sensitive areas.
Prereq: ENV S 200
Cross-listed as PLAN 368
Lab fee $10-15
Students may receive credit for only one of GEOG 368 and PLAN 368
Course Descriptions Geography

courses.label: GEOG 375
paras: Air Photo interpretation The principles of air photo interpretation utilizing specific criteria visible in the conventional air photo. Examples from local and foreign environments. Prereq: GEOG 275 and GEOG 201 Lab fee $20

courses.label: GEOG 376
courses.title: Environmental Remote Sensing
paras: Analysis of non-photographic systems of remote sensing (e.g. radar, landsat, SPOT). Study of remote sensing methods and data processing for analysis of physical and human environments.
Prereq: GEOG 275
Lab fee $10-$15

courses.label: GEOG 381
courses.title: The Nature of Geography
paras: The roots and evolution of geographic thought, conceptual approaches and pathways. Past traditions, current issues, and future trends. The politics and sociology of geography as an art, science, and profession.
Prereq: Third or fourth year geagraphy students

courses.label: GEOG 390
courses.title: Honours Thesis Proposal
paras: The development of a research proposal under the supervision of an appropriate faculty member. Normally taken in the third year. Students considering a topic demanding questionnaire data should take GEOG 307 in third year.
Prereq: Honours Geography students only

courses.label: GEOG 391
courses.title: Field Research
paras: One week field camp in which a specific area will be analysed from a geographic point of view. Individual or group analysis of specific field problems. General students may take this course only in fourth year.
Prereq: Honours or fourth year Geography students only
Estimated cost to student: $175.

courses.label: GEOG 401
courses.title: Glacial Geomorphology and Some Contemporary Applications
paras: Glacial and fluvioglacial erosion and deposition and their effects on landscapes. Focus on the environmental influences of glaciation and on practical applications of glacial geomorphologists’ techniques and information. Prereq: One of GEOG 300, EARTH 342

courses.label: GEOG 403
courses.title: Computer Asssisted Cartography
paras: Examination of spatial data processing and computer mapping techniques. Emphasis on digital terrain models and thematic mapping applications. Prereq: GEOG 160 and ENV S 278 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 409
courses.title: Energy Balance Climatology
paras: A field and lecture course including the radiation and energy balances of various surfaces, the principles of turbulent energy exchange, and the biotic response to the energy environment. These concepts will be illustrated through the collection and examination of field data. A self-directed learning approach is emphasized in this course. Prereq: GEOG 309

courses.label: GEOG 411
courses.title: Geography of Manufacturing Firms and Industries
paras: A companion course to GEOG 311. Emphasis on decision-making, multinational corporations, technological change, and analysis of the locational patterns of specific industries.
Prereq: GEOG 202A and GEOG 2028 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 421A
courses.title: Western Europe 1
paras: Physical, cultural, economic and poiitical geography of Europe north of the Alps. Topics such as the development of cities, problems of agriculture, changing industrial patterns, distribution of trade, regional disparities, environmental degradation, and planning on the city, regional and national levels, will be discussed.

courses.label: GEOG 421B
courses.title: Western Europe 2
paras: Physical, cultural, economic and political geography of Europe south of the Alps. Topics such as the development of cities, problems of agriculture, changing industrial patterns, distribution of trade, regional disparities, environmental degradation, and planning on the city, regional and national levels, will be discussed.

courses.label: GEOG 422
courses.title: Canada
paras: Seminar on geographical regional synthesis as applied to Canada. Study of regions at different scales. issues of continuing Canadian concern. A selfdirected learning approach is emphasized in this course.
Prereq: GEOG 322

courses.label: GEOG 450
courses.title: City and Regional Systems
paras: A continuation of Geography 349 and 350 with an emphasis on student projects.
Prereq: GEOG 350 and GEOG 349 or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 451
courses.title: Soils Geography
paras: An analysis of factors affecting soll
development and classification. Tech-
niques of soil survey and land classifi-
cation. Emphasis on fieldwork. Special
emphasis on surface mining rehabilita-
tion techniques. Urban and rural issues.
Past approaches and future needs. Prereq: GEOG 201

courses.label: GEOG 461
courses.title: Land Dereliction and Rehabilitation
paras: Reasons for land dereliction, its processes, and effects. .
Prereq: Fourth-year Environmental Studies students or consent of instructor

courses.label: GEOG 470
courses.title: Applied Alr Photo Interpretation
paras: Advanced air photo interpretation and its application in geomorphology, geology, resources inventory, engineering soils, hydrology and preplanning studies (terrain analysis). Projects in specific fields of interest form a significant part of the course.
Prereq: GEOG 375 and GEOG 300 or consent of instructor
Lab fee: $15-30

courses.label: GEOG 471
courses.title: Advanced Remote Sensing
paras: Principles of earth resource analysis using remotely sensed imagery and digital data with emphasis upon satellite platform sources. The coordination of supplemental imagery and ground truth missions with satellite data in a multistrategy perspective.
Prereq: GEOG 376
Lab fee $10-$15.

courses.label: GEOG 475A
courses.title: Each Independent Study of Selected Topics
paras: Individual study of specific topics not covered in other courses. Students must develop a brief outline to be filed with the Associate Chairman, Undergraduate Studies. A faculty member must agree to supervise the study. Prereq: Third- or fourth-year geogfaphy students and consent of instructor The fetter designation allows this course to be taken more than once for credit
Course Descriptions Geography

courses.label: GEOG 490A
courses.title: Honours Thesis Preparation
paras: Preparatory work and first draft of thesis.
Prereq: GEOG 390; only fourth year Honours students
A letter grade for GEOG 490A will be submitted only after the completion of GEOG 490B.

courses.label: GEOG 490B
courses.title: Honours Thesis Completion
paras: Completion of thesis.
Prereq: GEOG 390 and GEOG 490A; only fourth year Honours Students

Aniireg. Siudenis wiih HLTH 740 and/or 141 may not take this course for credit

courses.label: HLTH 210
courses.title: Growth, Development and Aging
paras: The physiology of human growth, development and aging is examined, with special reference to the influence of diet, environment, exercise and disease on ihe normal processes. Prereq: BIOL 230, 273 (Formerly BIOL 233)
Cross-listed
as KIN 210

courses.label: HLTH 220
courses.title: Health and the Family
paras: The course focuses on the family as the basic social unit responsible for the development and maintenance of the effective physical and mental health of its members. The interaction of biological, psychological, and socio-cultural factors will be considered as the family is examined using a lifespan approach. Prereg: HLTH 101/102 or 140/141, PSYCH 101 and Recommended SOC 101

courses.label: HLTH 245
courses.title: Community Health
paras: This course examines the Canadian health care system by considering organizational principles, health resources, service utilization, health care planning and health promotion strategies. There is a focus on societal and political issues which affect the health of the society through the delivery system.
Prereq: Health Studies students only or permission of instructor

courses.label: HLTH 340
courses.title: Environmental Health
paras: An introduction to the basic biological and toxicological processes that determine the effects of environmental pollutants on human health. Emphasis is placed on the mechanisms that give rise to chronic or delayed health effects, such as cancer, genetic mutations, and birth defects.
Prereq: KIN 317 or equivalent

courses.label: HLTH 341
courses.title: Disease Process
paras: An introduction to the study of biological factors governing the occurrence of disease in humans, using selected diseases to illustrate disease mechanisms and identification of risk factors. The means by which disease is induced and the host response are emphasized. The role that behaviour has in moditying biological response to disease is also considered.
Prereq: BIO! 230, 273 (Formerly BIOL 233), KIN 317 or equivalent
Course Descriptions Health Studies

courses.label: HLTH 344
courses.title: Program Evaluation
paras: A comprehensive and systematic introduction to the key concepts, methodologies, and issues related to program evaluation in general and their application to health programs in particular. Administrative and policy implications as well as the technical/methodological evaluation issues that face individuals involved in administering, planning, implementing, and evaluating health programs will be discussed.
Prereq: Basic courses in Statistics and in Research Design

courses.label: HLTH 346
courses.title: Nutrition
paras: An elementary course in nutrition with
special emphasis on diet for sport and
certain physiological conditions. Cross-listed as KIN 346

courses.label: HLTH 348
courses.title: Social Psychology of Health Behaviour
paras: The study and application of basic social psychological processes in relation to selected health-related behaviours (e.g. family planning, overeating, smoking, non-medical drug use, cardiovascular risk factors, patient compliance, medical care utilization). Prereq: PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor Cross-listed as KIN 348

courses.label: HLTH 349
courses.title: Principles of Behaviour Modification
paras: An overview of behaviour modification principles and procedures. Basic principles of reinforcement, punishment, _modelling and desensitization are examined as they relate to health behaviour.
Prereg; PSYCH 101 or consent of instructor
Cross-listed as KIN 349

courses.label: HLTH 350
courses.title: Occupational Health
paras: Methodological approaches to the detection, assessment and management of toxic hazards (especially carcinogens) in the workplace and external environment. The health effects of chemical toxicants on specific human organ systems (lung, nervous system, immune system, etc.) are also examined.
Prereq: HLTH 340, or permission of instructor

courses.label: HLTH 407
courses.title: Physiology of Coronary Hea’ Disease 7
paras: An examination of the pathology, risk factors and rehabilitation programs telated to coronary heart disease. Major emphasis is placed on the cardiorespiratory implications of exercise in the rehabilitation process.
Prereq: KIN 300 or permission of instructor
Cross-listed as KIN 407

courses.label: HLTH 431
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. Includes an approved proposal and completion of the first 3 chapters of the thesis — Introduction, Review of Literature, and Methods. Recommended for students planning graduate studies. Offering is contingent on the availability of resources.

courses.label: HLTH 432
courses.title: Research Project
paras: An independent research project on an approved topic, supervised by a faculty member. Includes data collection, data analysis and presentation of results in thesis form.
Prereq: Completion of HLTH 431
Recommended for students planning graduate studies.
Offering is contingent on the avait ability of resources.

courses.label: HLTH 433
courses.title: Advanced Research Project
paras: A course designed to familiarize students with the skills requisite for the formulation, execution and written presentation of an empirical research project. After a general discussion of the pertinent issues, students will be asked to analyse independently a data set related to a topic of interest to Health Studies students and to present this in the form of a research report. Prereq: KIN 222, 330 and CS 316 Students must be enrolled in either fourth-year regular or 3B Co-op of the Heaith Studies program.

courses.label: HLTH 442
courses.title: Epidemiology of Chronic Diseases
paras: An investigation of the epidemiology of selected chronic non-communicable diseases. The course emphasizes understanding of epidemiologic methods and identification of risk factors.
Prereq: An introductory statistics course or consent of instructor

courses.label: HLTH 443
courses.title: Behaviour and Chronic Disease
paras: A critical analysis of various behavioural strategies for the prevention of coronary heart disease, hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and lung cancer. The role of behaviour in the pathogenesis of disease and the feasiblity of behavioural change for prevention of disease will be discussed. Prereq: HLTH 344, 348, 349

courses.label: HLTH 445
courses.title: Seminar in Health Promotion
paras: A study of current issues pertaining to health promotion, health behaviour, or biomedical research. Topics may include pertinent research that is signifi- Cant to the health of individuals, famities and groups, or the community. Prereq: Health Studies students only Normally only fourth-year students will be admitted.

courses.label: HLTH 472
courses.title: Independent Study
paras: For the student who desires to pursue a particular topic in depth through guided independent research and/or reading. A faculty member must approve a student's project prior to registration. May be repeated in subsequent terms. Depending on student demand and availability of teaching resources, special topics may be presented to small groups in a lecture format. Such topics have included Pharmacology, Behavioural Immunity, Nutrition, The Health Care System.
Prereq: Consult with the Department
Course Descriptions Health Studies

courses.label: HIST 100
courses.title: Landmarks in World History
paras: A thematic introduction to the development of the world's major civilizations.

courses.label: HIST 102C
courses.title: The Origins of Wars in the Twentieth Century
paras: An analysis of the diplomatic, political, economic, ideological, social and cultural explanations of the causes of the major wars of this century with special emphasis on Canada.

courses.label: HIST 102E
courses.title: Canadian History
paras: Selected major themes from pioneer life to Canadian involvement in 20th century wars.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 102F
paras: An introduction to Western Intellectual History Since the Renaissance An exploration of some of the questions and answers posed by thinkers on the human predicament from Renaissance and Reformation times to the modern period. Readings range from Luther to J.P. Sartre, Shakespeare to Marx and Freud.
Taught in French in the 1992 Spring Term.

courses.label: HIST 102M
courses.title: Law and Society in the Middle Ages
paras: 500-1000 A study of the laws and legal! procedures of the Early Middle Ages. Anglo- Saxon and Germanic jaw will be examined along with legal procedures and institutions of that era.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 130
courses.title: The Modern World in Historical Perspective
paras: This course will introduce students, through interrelationships and interaction of selected themes, to contempotary history. Its format includes two interpretive lectures per week plus major films on 20th century crises and discussion groups.

courses.label: HIST 200
courses.title: Twentieth Century History as Documented by Films
paras: A history of the 20th century through films. The First World War, Europe between the Wars, the Second World War, North American society in the 20th century and other political, moral and social themes will be explored.

courses.label: HIST 204
courses.title: Life on the Ontario Frontier
paras: The course examines the cultural, moral, social and economic adaptations of European settlers to the Upper Canadian frontier environment.

courses.label: HIST 210
courses.title: History of Law
paras: An historical introduction to law in the
Ancient world. Babylonian, Assyrian.
Hittite and Roman law and legal prac-
tices and concepts will be examined. Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 211
courses.title: British History to 1603
paras: A survey of the main stages in the transition of Britain from a remote province of the Roman Empire to a prominent state of post-Reformation Europe. Within the chronological framework, political and constitutional as well as ecclesiastical and social developments will be examined.
This course is primarily intended for non-history majors. History majors may wish to take one or more of HIST 305, 307 and 308

courses.label: HIST 212
courses.title: British History Since 1603
paras: A survey of the shaping of British society and the British experience from the time of Shakespeare to the present; constitutional conflict and compromise, rise and fall of empire, industrial and urban revolution, world wars and welfare state.
This course is primarily intended for non-history majors. History majors may wish to take one or more of HIST 305, 307 and 308

courses.label: HIST 215
courses.title: The Proper Sphere: Canadian Women in Historical Perspective
paras: This course will examine the history of women in Canada from New France to the present day. The course will focus on the inter-relationship between women and their society, particularly as it affects the issues of work, health, reform and tegal status.

courses.label: HIST 218
courses.title: German History 1740-1945
paras: The development of Germany from the
Austrian-Prussian rivalry of 1740
through to the end of World War Il. Offered at Conrad Grebel College

courses.label: HIST 219
courses.title: Survey of Russian History
paras: An introductory survey treating the historical themes that contributed to the emergence of Russia, the Russian Empire, and the Soviet Union. Lectures, films and special presentations.

courses.label: HIST 221
courses.title: Race Relations in Canada: An Historical Perspective
paras: The “race problem” has appeared on the Canadian public agenda for the 1980's, but the issue is not of recent origin. This course will examine Euro- Canadian attitudes and practices toward non-European minorities from pioneer times to the present, and will set racial policies in the context of the evolution of a Canadian national iden-
tity.

courses.label: HIST 222
courses.title: History of Modern Revolutions
paras: An introduction to historical explanations of revolutions with special focus on social change and revolutionary theories. The French, Russian and Chinese Revolutions will be used as case studies.
Offered at Conrad Grebe! College.

courses.label: HIST 235
courses.title: History of Christianity
paras: The development of Christianity in its Raman Catholic, Eastern Orthodox and Protestant traditions from the time of Christ to the present. Offered at St. Jerome's College. Cross-listed as R S 230

courses.label: HIST 239
courses.title: History of Modern China, 1911 to the Present
paras: Some of the topics studied in this course include: the three stages of warlordism, the May Fourth Movement and the structure of society in the People's Republic of China.

courses.label: HIST 240
courses.title: Twentieth-Century Japanese History
paras: This course will examine the historical influences, both domestic and foreign, which led Japan to follow the course which has brought it to the present status of a powerful Asian nation.
Course Descriptions History

courses.label: HIST 241
courses.title: Society and the Sexes in Early Modern Europe
paras: This course will examine the changing importance of gender roles from the 15th to the 18th centuries. It will focus on topics such as sexuality, marriage, the family and the role of women in society and the work force.

courses.label: HIST 247
courses.title: Mennonite History: A Survey
paras: This course covers Mennonite origins, teachings, migrations, settlement patterns, divisions, leaders, institutions, and religious and social practices, indeed all facets of Mennonite history in various national settings.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 249
courses.title: History of Canadian-American Relations Since 1914
paras: An examination of the history of relations between the two countries since 1914. Topics of a political, economic, social and cultural nature will be studied.

courses.label: HIST 250
courses.title: The Art and Craft of History
paras: This course will provide a collegial learning setting within which students will be introduced to techniques of historical writing and research, and some examples of the best of recent historical scholarship.
Highly recommended for Year Two History majors.

courses.label: HIST 253
courses.title: Canadian History: The Colonial Period
paras: This course examines the major themes in pre-Contederation Canadian history including the rise and fall of New France, the creation of British North American societies in the Maritimes and Upper Canada and economic and political development.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 254
courses.title: Canadian History: The National Period
paras: This course examines Confederation, the rise of political parties, Canadian external relations, western discontent, the impact of both world wars and political and economic changes in Canada since 1945.
Offered at St. Jerome's College .

courses.label: HIST 255
courses.title: The Expansion of England
paras: The history of the British Empire down to the American War of Independence, telling the story of the Tudor seadogs, of the plantation of Ireland, the settlement of the North American mainland, the establishment of slave plantations in the Caribbean, and the earliest British enterprises in Africa, Asia and the Pacific.

courses.label: HIST 256
courses.title: The British Empire and Commonwealth
paras: The history of British imperialism. between the loss of the American colonies and the Falklands islands War of 1982, tracing the rise of the settlement colonies to dominion status, the huge expansion of the dependent empire during the age of the New Imperialism, the imperial apogee after World War |, and the rapid change from Empire to New Commonwealth after World War II.

courses.label: HIST 257
courses.title: The United States to 1900
paras: From the British provincial society of the 18th century to the emergence of modern America. Special emphasis on the American character, and on the moral dilemmas of republicanism and democracy, freedom and slavery, equality and competition.

courses.label: HIST 258
courses.title: America: Twentieth Century
paras: An analysis of two major themes: how America managed political reform and social change at home, and its emergence as a world power.

courses.label: HIST 259
courses.title: Modern African History
paras: An issue-oriented examination of some of the major developments in African political, social and economic history in the 20th century.

courses.label: HIST 260
courses.title: Europe: 814-1303
paras: The political, cultural, economic and ecclesiastical development of Europe from Charlemagne to Philip IV of France.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 263
courses.title: Europe: 1789-1945
paras: The growth of nationalism and nation states since the French revolution with attention to the Industrial Revolution, the World Wars, Fascism, Naziism and Stalinism.
Taught in French in the 1991 Spring term.

courses.label: HIST 273
courses.title: Canadian Social History |
paras: This course will cover the period from the early settlement of Canada to the beginnings of urban industrial develapment. Focus will be on the experiences of Canadians in their daily lives.

courses.label: HIST 274
courses.title: Canadian Social History II
paras: The social and cultural development of Canada irom the late nineteenth century to the present day.

courses.label: HIST 300
courses.title: The Idea of History
paras: The course is an introduction to the Philosophy of History and to historiography from the 19th century to the present. It deals with the great theoretical issues influencing historical analysis and with the classics of historical literature.
Highly recommended for Year Three History majors.

courses.label: HIST 304
courses.title: Medieval Church History
paras: An exploration of the development of the Church from 604 to 1449, Topics will include leadership struggles in church and state, crusades, heresy and inquisition, the western schism and the conciliar period. Offered at St. Jerome's College Cross-listed as R S 325

courses.label: HIST 307
courses.title: British History 1760-1867
paras: A study of people, power, thought and culture in the world's first industrializing society.

courses.label: HIST 308
courses.title: Britain Since 1867
paras: A study of the British experience and of Britain's part in world history from the 1860's to the 1980's.

courses.label: HIST 321
paras: Race Relations in Modern History: Case Studies

A detailed analysis of topics in the history of race relations intended primatily for students who have completed HIST 221 or other background to the subject. Special attention will be paid to revolutionary developments since World War Il, and to the emergence of modern human rights policies.

courses.label: HIST 325
courses.title: History of Canadian indians to
paras: “From Freedom to Conquest”. The history of Indian-white contact and its effect on the life and culture of the native Canadians.
Course Descriptions History

courses.label: HIST 326
courses.title: History of Canadian indians Since
paras: “Life under coercion” and the “New Indian”. The history of Indians on reserves and under government administration. Contemporary themes and issues of concer to native people are examined.

courses.label: HIST 339
courses.title: The History of France in the Nineteenth Century
paras: A study of French society and the four revolutions that influenced it with particular attention to social and institutional forces.

courses.label: HIST 340
courses.title: Europe: 1789-1914
paras: This course will examine European society amidst the dramatic changes of the nineteenth century. l(t will consider class, the family, gender, religion, and institutions during this century of political and social transformation.

courses.label: HIST 346
courses.title: Mennonite History: Special Topics
paras: A study of the Mennonite experience in Russia.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College

courses.label: HIST 348
courses.title: The Radical Reformation
paras: A study of 16th century Anabaptism —
a religious Reformation movement
dissenting from both Protestantism and
Roman Catholicism — its origins, its
social political and theological content.
and its relationship to such independent
dissenters as Sebastian Franck. Offered at Conrad Grebel College. Cross-listed as R S 322

courses.label: HIST 350
courses.title: British West Indian History
paras: A survey history of the British Caribbean, widely defined. Topics emphasized include early colonization, plantations, slave society, abolition and emancipation, the growth of nationalism, independence, and the roots of contemporary problems.

courses.label: HIST 355
courses.title: Russian History to 1900
paras: The course will focus on selected themes in the development of Muscovite and Imperial Russia from pre-tsarist times to the beginning of the 20th century.

courses.label: HIST 356
paras: 20th-Century Russia
The course will focus on selected themes in Russia's development in the 20th century including the Soviet period.

courses.label: HIST 358
courses.title: The History of Modern Germany
paras: From the Weimar Republic to
Reconstruction
A study of Germany from the rise of the
Nazis through the War experience, the
post-War settlement, the integration of
the refugees, the division into East and
West, and the economic miracle. Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 379
courses.title: Reformation History
paras: A study of the major sixteenth-century reformers and their intellectual background in humanism and late medieval scholasticism. Special attention will be given to the Lutheran and Reformed traditions and their ideological, social, political expressions.
Offered at Conrad Grebel College.

courses.label: HIST 385
courses.title: Canada: From MacDonald to Laurier
paras: An analytical and historical examination of the development of the Canadian nation from Confederation to the First World War.
Offered at St. Jerome's College

courses.label: HIST 387
courses.title: Ontario History since Confederation
paras: The course will examine the emergence of Ontario as an industrial giant and the development of its hegemony in Canada. An emphasis will also be placed on the sources and methods of local historical research.

courses.label: HIST 389
courses.title: Canada In World Affairs: From Laurier to Trudeau
paras: An analytical and historical examination of Canadian foreign policy in the international system, Domestic sources of Canadian foreign policy and international sources of Canadian foreign policy are examined in detail.

courses.label: HIST 396
courses.title: The History of the American South
paras: This course traces the main eras and issues in Southern history trom the 16th century to the mid-20th century. Topics examined will include pre-revolutionary and antebellum South, the Trial of Tears, the Civil War and reconstruction, the New South, the “lost cause”, the era of Jim Crow, and the search for the central theme.

courses.label: HIST 397
courses.title: Directed Studies In Special Topics
paras: Study in a limited field under tutorial guidance. A high standard of written work will be expected.

Senior Seminars

Each term of a senior seminar counts 1.0 credit. Seminars with the suffix “A” are reading seminars designed to give students an extensive acquaintance with scholarship in a particular field of history. Seminars with the suffix “B” are research seminars in which students will engage in research on particular topics in that field. Students should preregister for senior seminars, and for HIST 491, Independent Study in Special Subjects.
